 Head of the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Lieutenant General Kristomei Sianturi at the Evaluation Meeting for the Weather Modification Operation (OMO) in response to karhutla at the Integrated Post, Base Ops Halim Perdanakusumah, Jakarta, on Monday (2/11/2026). (Source: BNPB Screenshot) (Febrianto Adi Saputro) 
 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - The Head of the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB), Lieutenant General Kristomei Sianturi, evaluated the implementation of the Weather Modification Operation (OMO) in addressing forest and land fires (karhutla) that have been conducted in various regions across Indonesia.
 "This morning, I deliberately called everyone back together to listen to evaluations and to provide some directions on what we need to do moving forward," Kristomei stated while leading the Evaluation Meeting for the Weather Modification Operation (OMO) in response to karhutla at the Integrated Post, Base Ops Halim Perdanakusumah, Jakarta, on Monday (2/11/2026), as quoted in his remarks.
 Kristomei noted that this evaluation will help identify which areas still require OMO and which areas no longer need it.
 He expressed hope that the relocation or repositioning of OMO resources can be utilized in the regions that need them.
 "It has started to rain in South Sumatra, Jambi, Riau, or West Kalimantan, which we can assist first in the regions of Southeast Sulawesi and Central Sulawesi, including North Maluku and South Papua," Kristomei said.
 "If we can increase our support, we will shift resources where possible and add assets in those areas," he added.
 Anticipating Hydrometeorological Hazards
 Kristomei also highlighted the potential risks of hydrometeorological disasters predicted to occur during the rainy season forecasted by the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) to commence in late 2026.
 BNPB has issued Circular Letter No. 4 of 2026 regarding Preparedness Steps to Face the Rainy Season 2026/2027 on October 30, 2026.
 This circular was then distributed to governors, mayors, and regents throughout Indonesia, aimed at enhancing local governments' vigilance and readiness of personnel, equipment, and community capacity in their respective areas.
 "I also urge all governors, regents, and local leaders to be cautious regarding the risks of flooding in their respective areas," Kristomei mentioned.
 He emphasized that several regions have already experienced flooding.
 Therefore, he called on all parties to remain alert for the transition from dry season to rainy season.
 "The challenges appear to be shifting as well; after karhutla comes flooding. Let us anticipate this together," he remarked.
 The meeting was attended by the Head of BMKG, representatives from the military/police, as well as ministries/agencies and local governments, and was conducted in a hybrid format.
